block.txt: If the operator of a retirement village considers that an amendment to the village rules to which the residents have consented under section 51 will impose a cost on the operator additional to that allowed for in the approved annual budget, the operator must seek the residents’ consent to an amendment to the approved annual budget.

Division 5 of Part 7 provides for proposed and approved annual budgets. Section 117 allows an operator to seek the residents’ consent to an amendment to the approved annual budget if unforeseen requirements for expenditure arise.
Section 115 does not apply to or in respect of a consent sought under this section.
If the residents refuse to consent to the amendment, the operator may apply to the Tribunal for an order in relation to the proposed amendment to the approved annual budget.
On application to it under this section, the Tribunal may, after considering the circumstances of the case, either—
order that the approved annual budget be amended as specified in the order, or
order that the approved annual budget not be amended.
On making an order under subsection (4), the Tribunal may also—
order that the proposed amendment to the village rules is not to take effect, or
order that the proposed amendment to the village rules (or the proposed amendment modified as specified in the order) is to take effect from the date specified in the order.
This section does not apply in respect of a retirement village where the residents have consented under section 112 (7) to not being supplied with a proposed annual budget.

heading.b: Other applications to Tribunal concerning village rules

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village or a resident of the village may, at any time, apply to the Tribunal for an order in relation to either or both of the following—
a dispute concerning the legal validity of a village rule in force in the village,
a village rule in force in the village that the operator or resident considers to be unjust, unconscionable, harsh or oppressive.
The Tribunal may determine an application made under subsection (1) by making an order—
setting aside the village rule concerned, or
modifying the operation of the rule in its application to a resident or to some or all of the residents of the village, or
upholding the rule.
The operator and residents of a retirement village must comply with the village rules as in force from time to time.

The Tribunal can make various orders in relation to compliance with the village rules—see section 128. It can also terminate a resident’s residence contract for serious or persistent breaches of the village rules—see section 134.

If a village rule is inconsistent with a term of a village contract, the village rule prevails to the extent of the inconsistency. However, if the inconsistent term of the contract is a prescribed term, that term prevails over the rule.

heading.b: Compliance with village rules by persons other than operator and residents

block.txt: It is a term of every village contract that the resident or former occupant who is a party to the contract will use his or her best endeavours to ensure compliance with the village rules by—
a tenant or subtenant, under Division 5 of Part 10, of the resident or former occupant, and

any other person who is lawfully on the resident’s or former occupant’s residential premises (other than a person who has a right of entry to the premises without the resident’s or former occupant’s consent), and
any other person who is in the retirement village at the resident’s or former occupant’s invitation.
It is also a term of every village contract that the operator will use his or her best endeavours to ensure compliance with the village rules by—
tenants of the operator, and
employees of the operator, and
any other persons who are in the retirement village at the operator’s invitation.

heading.b: Certain persons not to be operators

block.txt: A person to whom this section applies must not—
be an operator of a retirement village, or
be involved in the promotion or sale of residence rights in a retirement village, or
be in any way (whether directly or indirectly) concerned, or take part, in the management or control of a retirement village.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
This section applies to the following persons—
a person who is insolvent under administration,
a person who is a director of a Chapter 5 body corporate,
a person who was a director of a company that has been wound up (otherwise than voluntarily),
a person who has been convicted (in New South Wales or elsewhere) of an offence involving—
physical violence to another person, or
fraud or dishonesty, being an offence punishable on conviction by imprisonment for a period of not less than 3 months.
However, this section applies—
to a person referred to in subsection (2) (c)—only for the period of 5 years immediately following the winding-up, and

to a person referred to in subsection (2) (d)—only for the period of 5 years following the conviction (or, if the person was sentenced to imprisonment, within the period of 5 years following the person’s release).

The Secretary may, on the application of a person who is a director of a Chapter 5 body corporate, exempt the person from the operation of this section if, on the basis of information provided to the Secretary by the person, the Secretary considers it appropriate to do so.
In this section, Chapter 5 body corporate and insolvent under administration have the same meanings as they have in the Corporations Act 2001 of the Commonwealth.
The operator of a retirement village must ensure that the village generally is reasonably secure.

In particular, the operator must ensure that all residential premises in the village have such locks or other security devices, in good working order, as are necessary to make the premises reasonably secure.

Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of residential premises that are subject to a community land scheme, company title scheme or strata scheme unless the operator, or a close associate of the operator, is the owner of the premises.
Any resident who believes in good faith that the retirement village is not reasonably secure may apply to the Tribunal for any of the following—
an order directing the operator to comply with subsection (1) or (2),
any other order referred to in section 128 (1).
The operator of a retirement village must ensure that the village generally is reasonably safe.
In particular, the operator must—
ensure that an emergency plan is prepared for the retirement village, and
ensure that the emergency plan is maintained so that it remains effective, and
take reasonable steps to ensure that all residents and staff are familiar with the emergency plan, and
undertake a safety inspection at least once each calendar year, and make a safety inspection report on the findings of any such inspection, and
ensure that residents are—
notified in writing when a safety inspection is undertaken, and
given access to the safety inspection report if they request it, and
take such other action as the regulations may require to ensure that the village generally is reasonably safe.
An operator commits an offence if the operator contravenes subsection (2) (a).
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 100 penalty units (in any other case).

Section 189B enables the Secretary to issue guidelines to assist operators in complying with their obligations under subsection (2) (a), (b) and (b1). The Tribunal may take guidelines into account in determining whether there has been compliance with those provisions.
The emergency plan for the purposes of subsection (2) (a) and (b) must provide for emergency procedures, including—
an effective response to an emergency, and
evacuation procedures, and
notifying emergency service organisations at the earliest opportunity, and
medical treatment and assistance, and
effective communication between the operator (or other person authorised by the operator to coordinate the emergency response) and all residents in the village.

In preparing and maintaining an emergency plan for the purposes of subsection (2) (a) and (b), the operator of the retirement village must have regard to all relevant matters, including the following—
the nature of the hazards in the village,
the size, location and layout of the village,
the number of residents in the village,
the evacuation arrangements required for residents with mobility, hearing, visual or other impairments.
Without limiting subsection (2) (e), the regulations may make provision for, or with respect to, the following—
the form of the emergency plan,
the conduct of safety inspections required under subsection (2) (c),
the manner and form of such a safety inspection report,
the manner and form for notifying and giving access to safety inspection reports for the purposes of subsection (2) (d).
Any resident who believes in good faith that the retirement village is not reasonably safe may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) any of the following—
an order directing the operator to comply with subsection (1) or (2),
any other order referred to in section 128 (1).

heading.b: Annual emergency evacuation exercises and key safety information display

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must ensure that—
an evacuation exercise for residents is carried out at least once each calendar year, and
key safety information is clearly displayed in communal areas within the retirement village, and
key safety information is provided to residents in relation to their residential premises within the retirement village.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 100 penalty units (in any other case).

Section 189B enables the Secretary to issue guidelines to assist operators in complying with their obligations under this section. The Tribunal may take guidelines into account in determining whether there has been compliance with this section.
Each of the following is key safety information for the purposes of subsection (1)—
a map indicating the location of assembly areas, exits and fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment for the communal areas and residential premises concerned,
instructions concerning the evacuation of residents and staff from the communal areas and residential premises concerned in the event of a fire or other emergency,
any other information of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following—
the conduct of evacuation exercises,
the display and provision of key safety information.
A resident of a retirement village who believes in good faith that the operator is contravening subsection (1) may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) any of the following—
an order directing the operator to comply with subsection (1),
any other order referred to in section 128 (1).
Nothing in this section limits the obligations of an operator of a retirement village under sections 58 and 58A.

heading.b: Operator to provide village emergency system on request

block.txt: The residents of a retirement village may, by a special resolution, request the operator of the village to provide or arrange for a village emergency system of a specified kind in the village.

If such a request is made, the residents are taken to have consented to the inclusion, in the proposed annual budget relating to the financial year next following the date of the resolution, of the cost of providing or arranging for the village emergency system concerned.

If the operator fails to comply with a request referred to in this section, any resident of the village may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing the operator to provide or arrange for a village emergency system of the kind requested by the residents.
The operator must ensure that any village emergency system provided in the village (whether or not it was provided at the request of the residents) is regularly and adequately monitored and serviced.

Nothing in this section prevents a resident of a retirement village from arranging, at the resident’s expense, for the provision of a system that will enable the resident to summon assistance in an emergency. However, any such system is not a village emergency system.

In this section, village emergency system means a system (such as buttons in residential premises and common areas, or bracelets that can be worn by residents) that enables residents to summon assistance in an emergency.

heading.b: Operator to provide emergency and home care service vehicles access to retirement village

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must take all reasonable steps to ensure that—
emergency and home care service personnel have unimpeded vehicular access to the residential premises in the village at all times, both by day and by night, and
the residents of the village, and local emergency and home care service agencies, are consulted and kept informed about any arrangements made to secure that access.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Variation in services or facilities provided at village

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must propose a variation in the services and facilities provided at the village if—

a minimum of 5 residents, or 10% of the residents, (whichever is the greater) of the village (or, if the village has fewer than 10 occupied residential premises, residents from a majority of the occupied residential premises), or
the Residents Committee of the village,
requests the operator in writing to do so.
The operator may propose a variation in the services and facilities provided at the village even if there has been no request under subsection (1).

The services and facilities provided at the village are not to be varied as proposed unless the residents of the village, by a special resolution, consent to the variation. If consent is given, the operator may vary the service or facility in accordance with the consent as soon as is practicable (unless the resolution provides that the variation is to take effect on a specified later date).

An operator who receives a request under subsection (1) must call a meeting of the residents of the village, to be held no later than 28 days after the receipt of the request, for the purpose of considering a special resolution concerning the proposed variation.
A resident is not entitled to vote on the special resolution unless the service or facility concerned is (or is proposed to be) available to the resident.
Regardless of the terms of any village contract, the operator does not breach the contract by varying services or facilities in accordance with this section.

If the operator considers that a proposed variation in services or facilities under this section will impose a cost on the operator additional to that allowed for in the approved annual budget, the operator must seek the residents’ consent to an amendment to the approved annual budget.
Section 115 does not apply to or in respect of a consent sought under this section.
If the residents refuse to consent to the amendment, section 53 (3)–(5) applies to such a refusal in the same way that it applies to a refusal under that section.
In this section—
services and facilities means services and facilities provided by or on behalf of the operator.
variation in a service or facility includes the following—
a reduction in the service or facility,
the withdrawal of a service or facility,
an increase in a service or facility,
any other change in a service or facility,
the provision of a new service or facility.

heading.b: Operator not to reduce or withdraw certain services and facilities

block.txt: If a development consent for a retirement village requires that a particular service or facility be provided for the life of the village, the operator of the village must not reduce or withdraw that service or facility (despite any consent of the residents) unless the development consent is amended so as to omit or vary that requirement.

heading.b: Consequence of unlawful variation in services or facilities

block.txt: If an operator reduces or withdraws, or permits the reduction or withdrawal of, a service or facility otherwise than in accordance with section 60, a resident of the village concerned may apply to the Tribunal for an order for any one or more of the following—
the reinstatement of the service or facility concerned,
the payment of compensation in relation to the reduced or withdrawn service or facility,
a reduction in the recurrent charges payable by any one or more of the residents,
the payment of the whole or part of those recurrent charges to the Tribunal until the service or facility concerned is reinstated.
In determining an application made under this section, the Tribunal may make the order sought or any other order of a kind set out in subsection (1).

heading.b: Operator not to require residents to patronise particular businesses

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must not restrict the right of a resident of the village to purchase goods and services from a person of the resident’s choice.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.
For example, the operator must not prevent a resident from obtaining meals-on-wheels services or any other service known as a Home and Community Care service (HACC).
However, the operator may prohibit particular tradespersons and service providers from entry (or further entry) into the village if they have—
unduly disturbed the peace and quiet of the village, or
failed to observe reasonable rules of conduct established by the operator, or
contravened any village rules concerning motor vehicle traffic that are displayed in, or near the boundary of, the village.

heading.b: Operator not to demand power of attorney

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must not require a resident or prospective resident of the village to give the operator a power of attorney in favour of the operator, a close associate of the operator or a person nominated by the operator.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

Any power of attorney given in favour of an operator of a retirement village (or a close associate of the operator or a person nominated by the operator) by a resident or prospective resident of the village—
if given before the commencement of this section—terminates on that commencement, and
if given on or after the commencement of this section—is void.
Subsection (2) does not apply if the resident or prospective resident who gave the power of attorney is a relative of the operator.
This section has effect despite the provisions of the Powers of Attorney Act 2003 and despite the terms of any instrument creating a power of attorney.

Part 3 of the Powers of Attorney Act 2003 deals with irrevocable powers of attorney. Division 2 of Part 4 of that Act deals with enduring powers of attorney that are given with the intention that they will continue to be effective even if the person who gave the power loses capacity through mental incapacity.

heading.b: Operator to respect rights of residents

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must respect the rights of residents of the village.
In particular, the operator—
must not interfere, or cause or permit any interference, with the reasonable peace, comfort or privacy of a resident, and

must take all reasonable steps to ensure that all residents meet their obligations under their village contracts, the village rules and this Act, so that a resident does not unreasonably interfere with the peace, comfort and quiet enjoyment of his or her fellow residents, and
must not interfere with the right of any resident to autonomy over his or her personal, financial and other matters and over his or her possessions, and
must not inhibit any resident from exercising self-reliance in matters relating to his or her personal, domestic and financial affairs, and
must use his or her best endeavours to ensure that each resident lives in an environment free from harassment and intimidation.

A resident of a retirement village who is of the opinion that the operator of the village has contravened any provision of this section in relation to the resident may apply to the Tribunal for an order for either or both of the following—
an order directing the operator to pay compensation to the resident,
an order directing the operator to comply with this section.
On an application made under this section, the Tribunal may make the order sought or any other order of a kind set out in subsection (3).

heading.b: Restriction of operator’s access to residential premises

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village and any person authorised by the operator must not, while a person has residence rights in relation to residential premises in the village, enter those residential premises except as permitted by this section.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
The operator or other person may enter residential premises in the village only in the following circumstances—
if the resident consents to the entry,
in an emergency, or if the operator has reasonable cause for concern about the health or safety of a person that the operator believes is on the premises,
in order to carry out urgent repairs,
in order to carry out general maintenance, but only if 7 days’ notice has been given to the resident,
in order to carry out a general inspection of the premises, but only if—
the resident is not a registered interest holder with respect to the premises, and
7 days’ notice has been given to the resident, and
a general inspection of the premises has not been carried out more than once in the immediately preceding 12 months,
in accordance with an order of the Tribunal,
in any other circumstances prescribed by the regulations.
The Tribunal may, on the application of the operator, make an order authorising the operator or any other person to enter residential premises in the village.

A resident of a retirement village who is of the opinion that the operator of the village has contravened any provision of this section in relation to the resident may apply to the Tribunal for an order for either or both of the following—
an order directing the operator to pay compensation to the resident,
an order directing the operator to comply with this section.
On an application made under subsection (4), the Tribunal may make the order sought or any other order of a kind set out in that subsection.

A resident of a retirement village may appoint a person as the resident’s agent for the purpose of receiving notices or other documents to be given to the resident under a village contract or under this Act.
A resident may wish to appoint an agent if the resident (for example) cannot read or write English, is sick, or is going to be away from his or her residential premises for some time.
An appointment of the operator of the retirement village (or a close associate of the operator or a person nominated by the operator) as an agent under this section is of no effect.
An appointment under this section—
may be made in a village contract or at any time after the contract commences, and
may be revoked at any time by the resident,
but any such appointment or revocation has no effect until it is notified in writing to the operator of the village.

The operator must give to the agent appointed by a resident, until such time as the appointment expires or is revoked, any notices or other documents that the operator is required to give to the resident under a village contract or this Act.
A notice or other document that is required by this section to be given to the agent appointed by the resident and that is not so given is taken not to have been given to the resident.

heading.b: Residents to be given access to information about them

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village—
must, on request at any reasonable time, give a resident access to any information about the resident that is held by the operator, and
must give the resident a copy of that information if the resident requests it, and
if the resident satisfies the operator that any of the information is incorrect—must correct the information, on request, in accordance with the resident’s instructions.
Section 197 prohibits an operator of a retirement village from charging the resident for giving access to the information or providing a copy of it.
If the operator fails to comply with a request made under this section, the resident concerned may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing the operator to comply.

heading.b: Right to request resident’s current village contract information meeting

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village, if requested in writing by a resident, must—
meet with the resident at least once each calendar year to explain the resident’s current village contract information, and
provide a written summary at the meeting of the explanation of the resident’s current village contract information.

Section 189B enables the Secretary to issue guidelines to assist operators in complying with their obligations under this section. The Tribunal may take guidelines into account in determining whether there has been compliance with this section.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 20 penalty units (in any other case).

The operator is not required to explain under subsection (1) (a) any information forming part of the resident’s current village contract information if the written request for the meeting indicates that the resident has waived an explanation of the information.
However, the operator must still include the information in the written summary provided under subsection (1) (b).

A resident may, in the written request for the meeting or by a further notice in writing given to the operator, nominate one or more persons to represent the resident at the meeting or to attend the meeting with the resident.
The operator must ensure that—
the resident or a nominated representative of the resident is provided with a written reply to a request for a meeting, and
if the resident is entitled to a meeting, the meeting is held within 30 days of the request for the meeting being received by the operator.
An operator commits an offence if the operator contravenes subsection (4) (b).
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 20 penalty units (in any other case).

The operator may, in the written reply provided under subsection (4) (a) or by a further notice in writing given to the resident or a nominated representative of the resident, nominate a person to conduct the meeting on behalf of the operator if the person is capable of explaining the resident’s current village contract information and answering questions about it.
A resident’s current village contract information for the purposes of this section is—
for a resident who is a registered interest holder—each of the following—
the requirements under this Act, the regulations and the village contract for terminating the village contract or selling the residential premises to which the contract relates,
the estimated departure fee (if any) payable by the resident,
the resident’s liability to pay recurrent charges under section 152,
estimates of any amounts payable by the resident in relation to the sale of the residential premises,
the estimated sale price for the residential premises,
the estimated amount that would be payable by the operator to the resident following the sale of the residential premises,
estimates of any other amounts payable by the resident under their village contract (including any amount of capital gain shared with the operator),
any other information concerning the resident’s rights or obligations (including after vacating the residential premises) of a kind prescribed by the regulations, or
for a resident who is not a registered interest holder—each of the following—
the requirements under this Act, the regulations and the village contract for terminating the village contract,
the estimated departure fee (if any) payable by the resident,
the resident’s liability to pay recurrent charges under section 153,
the estimated amount payable by the resident in respect of repairs required to the residential premises in accordance with section 163,
the estimated ingoing contribution that would be payable by an incoming resident of the residential premises where this contribution is material to the calculation of estimates under this section,
the estimated amount that would be payable by the operator to the resident following the residential premises being vacated by the resident,
estimates of any other amounts payable by the resident under their village contract (including any amount of capital gain shared with the operator),
any other information concerning the resident’s rights or obligations (including after vacating the residential premises) of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
The operator must ensure that estimated amounts for the purposes of subsection (7) are reasonable estimates that are calculated—
by reference to a stated date (being either the date of the meeting or a date that is not later than 30 days after the meeting), and
as if the stated date was the date on which the resident’s right to occupy the residential premises concerned terminated.
See sections 180 and 181 for the determination of amounts payable to former occupants.
An operator commits an offence if the operator provides an estimate for the purposes of subsection (7) that is not reasonable.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 100 penalty units (in any other case).
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to—
the form of a written summary for the purposes of subsection (1) (b), and
the keeping of records by operators or former operators of retirement villages concerning the calculation of estimated amounts for the purposes of subsection (7).

The Secretary may, by notice in writing given to an operator of a retirement village (an estimate calculation notice), require the operator to provide, within the period specified in the notice, evidence of the reasonableness of any estimate of an amount for the purposes of subsection (7) made for the purposes of a meeting under this section.
An operator of a retirement village who fails to comply with an estimate calculation notice within the period for compliance specified in the notice is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 100 penalty units (in any other case).
Any resident of a retirement village who believes in good faith that the operator is contravening this section may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) any of the following—
an order directing the operator to comply with a provision of this section,
any other order referred to in section 128 (1).
A Residents Committee may, with the consent of the residents of a retirement village, be established in the village for the purposes of this Act.
A Residents Committee is to be elected by the residents.
Only one Residents Committee may be established in a village, and only a resident of the village may be a member of the Committee.

If more than one body or committee (regardless of its name) purports to be the Residents Committee in a particular retirement village, the operator or a resident of the village may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order determining which body or committee (if any) is the Residents Committee for the village.
A Residents Committee may, subject to the regulations—
determine its own procedure, and
form any one or more sub-committees and determine their procedure, and
call meetings of all the residents of the village for the purpose of considering and voting on matters referred to in section 74 (1).
The operator of a retirement village must not—
discourage or prevent the establishment of a Residents Committee, or
obstruct a Residents Committee in the exercise of its functions, or
attempt to prevent residents of the village from joining any organisation for residents of retirement villages.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

The operator must provide reasonable administrative assistance to the Residents Committee on request by the Committee, but only if an estimate of the cost of providing the assistance has been included in the approved annual budget for the financial year in which the assistance is requested.
Administrative assistance might involve such matters as photocopying or distributing notices.
Nothing in this section prevents the residents of a retirement village from establishing other committees of residents for other purposes.

A person must not hold the same office, or hold an office performing the same (or substantially the same) functions, on the Residents Committee of a retirement village for more than 3 consecutive years, except as provided by the regulations.
The election of a person to an office in contravention of subsection (1) is void.

Any act, matter or thing done by a Residents Committee, in good faith, even though at the time that the act, matter or thing was done the election of a member of the Committee was void under subsection (2), is valid as if the election of the member was not void under that subsection.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the election, functions and procedure of Residents Committees and sub-committees.
The regulations may also prescribe model rules that may be adopted by a Residents Committee.

heading.b: Meetings between Residents Committee and operator

block.txt: An operator of a retirement village must, on the reasonable request of a Residents Committee, meet the Committee (or a representative of the Committee).
Subsection (1) does not apply to an operator who owns land in the village unless the operator is also involved in the management and control of the village.
A Residents Committee (or a representative of the Committee) must, on the reasonable request of the operator of the village concerned, meet the operator.

If a reasonable request under this section is not complied with, the operator or the Residents Committee that made the request may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing compliance with the request.

heading.b: Annual management meeting to be held by operator

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must hold, in each financial year of the retirement village, an annual management meeting of the residents of the retirement village in accordance with this section.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
The annual management meeting must be held not more than 4 months after the end of each financial year.
The annual management meeting must be chaired by—
the operator of the retirement village, or
a representative of the operator of the retirement village who is authorised to answer questions put at the meeting in accordance with this section.
The operator must notify the residents of the retirement village at least 14 days before the annual management meeting of—
the time of the meeting, and
the place at which the residents may attend the meeting in person, and
if the residents may attend the meeting by electronic means—details of how the residents can attend and participate in the meeting using the means, and
the agenda for the meeting.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
The notice referred to in subsection (4) must also include an invitation to the residents of the retirement village to submit—
written questions to the operator at least 7 days before the meeting, and
other questions at the meeting.
The regulations may prescribe matters that must be included in the agenda for an annual management meeting.

If the operator of the retirement village is required, by section 75 (2B) to be absent from any part of the meeting, the meeting is to be chaired by a resident agreed upon by the residents at the meeting for that purpose.

If the residents are given the option of attending the meeting by electronic means, the chair of the meeting must take reasonable steps to ensure each resident or former occupant can participate in, and vote at, the meeting using the means.
Nothing in this section prevents the operator of a retirement village from calling a meeting of the residents of the retirement village at any other time.

For the avoidance of doubt, the annual management meeting is a meeting of the residents of a retirement village and, accordingly, the provisions of this Act applying to meetings of the residents also apply to an annual management meeting.

heading.b: Questions to be answered at annual management meeting

block.txt: The chair of the annual management meeting must ensure that the residents of a retirement village have a reasonable opportunity to put questions to the operator of the retirement village or a representative of the operator at the meeting.
The operator of a retirement village or representative of the operator must answer questions submitted in writing (under section 72A (5) (a)) or put to the operator or representative at the meeting—
if possible—in reasonable detail at the relevant meeting, and

to the extent that compliance with paragraph (a) is not possible—in reasonable detail, as soon as is practicable after the meeting, in a notice in writing given to all of the residents of the retirement village.
Nothing in this section requires the operator or a person representing the operator to—
answer an unreasonable question, or
answer a question relating to a matter that is prescribed by the regulations as an excluded matter for the purposes of this section.
If there is no Residents Committee elected for a retirement village, the operator of the village must call a meeting of the residents (to be held in or near the village) if requested to do so by—
in the case of a retirement village with fewer than 10 occupied residential premises—residents from a majority of the occupied residential premises, or
in the case of a retirement village with 10 or more occupied residential premises—the greater of—
5 residents of the retirement village, or
10% of the residents of the retirement village.
The residents of a retirement village have the right to meet for the purpose of considering and voting on—
any matter in respect of which the consent of the residents is required under this Act, and
any other matter affecting the management and operation of the village, and
any matter prescribed by the regulations.
A vote of the residents on a matter referred to in subsection (1) (b) does not bind the operator of the village.
If 2 or more residents occupy the same residential premises in the village, each of them may vote on a matter referred to in subsection (1).
The operator of the retirement village must not interfere with a resident’s rights under this section.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
A meeting of residents must not be held simultaneously with a meeting that the residents, in another capacity, are required to hold or participate in under another Act.
An example of such a meeting is a meeting required by the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 (if the retirement village is subject to a strata scheme).
A resident of a retirement village is not obliged to attend, or vote at, any meeting of the residents of the village.

A person (other than a duly-appointed proxy of a resident) who is not a resident of the village (including a person who occupies residential premises in the village otherwise than under a residence right) must not attend, or remain at, a meeting of the residents unless the residents at the meeting consent to the person’s presence at the meeting.
Subsection (2) does not apply to the operator of a retirement village, or a person representing the operator of a retirement village, during the annual management meeting of the retirement village.

The operator or operator’s representative must not be present at a meeting of residents during the casting of any vote that is to be taken by the residents at the meeting, but may return to the meeting after the vote has been cast.
Despite subsection (2), a person has a right to attend a meeting of the residents of a retirement village and to vote at the meeting on behalf of a resident of the village if the person—
is authorised to do so under a power of attorney given in favour of the person by the resident concerned, or

is a person appointed, under the Guardianship Act 1987 or the NSW Trustee and Guardian Act 2009, to manage the estate of the resident (or, if the management of the resident’s estate is committed to the NSW Trustee and Guardian, the person is the NSW Trustee and Guardian or a person authorised by the NSW Trustee and Guardian for the purposes of this section).

The operator of the retirement village must not prevent or hinder the attendance of an investigator at a meeting of the residents if the residents at the meeting consent to the investigator’s presence at the meeting.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

A village contract may explain the system under which, at the time the contract is entered into, the residents of the retirement village meet and consider and vote on matters referred to in section 74 (1), but any term of the contract that purports to bind a resident to a particular system is void to the extent that it does so.

Any covenant, and any contract or other arrangement between the operator of a retirement village and a resident of the village, under which a particular vote of the resident (or the resident’s failure to vote) on any matter relating to the village attracts a penalty, is void to the extent of that provision.
A resident of a retirement village may, from time to time, appoint a person as the proxy of the resident.
Any such appointment is to be made in the form and manner prescribed by the regulations.
A person is not the proxy of a resident of a retirement village for the purposes of this Act unless the person is appointed under this section.

Certain other laws (such as the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015) provide for the appointment of proxies for various purposes. However, an appointment under another law is not effective for the purposes of this Act, and an appointment under this Act is not effective for the purposes of another law (unless the other law provides that it is).
An appointment of the operator of a retirement village or close associate of the operator of a retirement village as a proxy is of no effect.
A person appointed as the proxy of a resident of a retirement village cannot vote on the resident’s behalf if the resident personally votes on the matter concerned.
This section has effect despite any terms of the instrument appointing a person as the proxy of the resident.

If a person holds appointments as the proxy of 2 residents (or such other number of residents as may be prescribed by the regulations) in any one retirement village at any one time, any appointment of the person as proxy of another resident of the village, while the person continues to hold the other appointments, is void.
Any appointment of a person as the proxy of a resident of a retirement village after the commencement of this section—
may be revoked at any time by the appointor’s giving notice in writing to the person, and
if it is not revoked, terminates—
after the first meeting at which it is exercised, or
if it is not exercised during the period of 6 months immediately following the date on which the appointment is made—on the expiry of that period.
Nothing in this section prevents a resident of a retirement village from reappointing a person as the resident’s proxy after the revocation or termination of such an appointment.
Any vote or resolution of the residents of a retirement village that purports to oblige the operator of the village concerned—
to abandon or amend plans for development in the village, or
to cease to act as the operator of the village,
is not binding on the operator.
Submissions concerning proposed development in the village can be made under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 at the time that the operator seeks development consent under that Act.

Retirement villages may contain residential premises that are subject to a company title scheme, to a community scheme, precinct scheme or neighbourhood scheme under the Community Land Management Act 2021, or to a strata scheme under the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015. Resolutions of directors or members of the companies, and votes of relevant associations (under the Community Land Management Act 2021) and owners corporations (under the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015) have no relevance to decisions of residents under this Act (and vice versa).

The maximum notice of an intention to vacate residential premises in a retirement village that may be required of a resident of the premises (whether under a contract or otherwise) is one month’s notice in writing.

heading.b: Right of certain non-residents to become residents

block.txt: A relative of a resident of residential premises in a retirement village—
who is a retired person, and
who is occupying the residential premises concerned at the time that the resident dies or vacates the premises, and
who had been occupying those premises for at least 6 months (whether before or after the commencement of this Act) immediately before that time,
has the right to enter into a residence contract with the operator of the village in respect of the premises.
This section does not apply if—
the resident is, or was, a registered interest holder (other than a person referred to in section 7 (1) (c)) in respect of the residential premises, or
the resident is taken to be a resident by operation of section 4 (2).

If the operator of a retirement village refuses to enter into a residence contract referred to in section 81, the relative of the resident may apply to the Tribunal for an order directing the operator of the village to enter into the contract within the time specified in the order.
If the relative of the resident—
refuses to enter into a residence contract with the operator of the village in respect of the residential premises concerned, and
refuses to deliver vacant possession of the residential premises to the operator,
the operator may apply to the Tribunal for an order directing the relative of the resident to deliver vacant possession of the premises to the operator within the time specified in the order.
On an application made to it under this section, the Tribunal may make the order sought or any other order of a kind referred to in this section, as the Tribunal considers appropriate.

If the Tribunal is satisfied that the relative of the resident refused to enter into a residence contract only because the terms of the proposed contract were unreasonable, the Tribunal may set the terms of the contract (having regard to the terms of other residence contracts in force in the village) and direct the operator and the relative of the resident to enter into the contract within the time specified in the order.
The operator of the village must not enter into a residence contract in respect of the residential premises with any person other than the relative of the resident unless—
the relative delivers vacant possession of the premises to the operator, or
the Tribunal orders the relative to do so.
A contract entered into in contravention of subsection (5) is void.
If—
a person who was occupying residential premises in the retirement village with a resident who has vacated the premises is not a person referred to in section 81 (1), and
the person refuses to deliver vacant possession of the premises to the operator,

the operator may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order requiring the person to deliver vacant possession of the premises to the operator within the time specified in the order.

heading.b: Residents to respect rights of other persons

block.txt: It is a term of every residence contract that the resident will respect the rights of other residents of, and other persons in, the village.
In particular, a resident—
must not interfere, or cause or permit any interference, with the reasonable peace, comfort or privacy of another resident, and
must respect the rights of the operator of the village, and agents and employees of the operator, to work in an environment free from harassment or intimidation, and
must not act in a manner that adversely affects the occupational health and safety of persons working in the village.

If the operator of the retirement village is of the opinion that a resident of the village has contravened any provision of this section, the operator may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing the resident to comply with this section.
In this Division—
rules of conduct means rules of conduct prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of section 83B.

heading.b: Rules of conduct for operators may be prescribed by regulations

block.txt: The regulations may prescribe rules of conduct for operators for or with respect to professionalism, training, competencies, performance and behaviour in connection with the management or operation of retirement villages.
Without limiting subsection (1), rules of conduct may make provision for or with respect to the following—
knowledge about—
the provisions of this Act and the regulations, and
the provisions of the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 and the regulations under that Act relevant to the management or operation of retirement villages, and
any other law relevant to the management or operation of retirement villages,
conduct in relation to dealings with current or prospective residents of retirement villages (for example, by reference to standards of honesty, fairness and professionalism),
conduct in relation to the marketing of retirement villages (including in relation to the use of terminology),
internal dispute resolution measures used in retirement villages,
training and competencies for operators of retirement villages and their staff.

heading.b: Contravention of offence provisions of rules of conduct

block.txt: An operator must not contravene a provision of the rules of conduct that is identified by the rules as an offence provision.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 50 penalty units (in any other case).
The Secretary may apply to the Supreme Court, in accordance with the rules of the Court, for an order appointing a specified person as an administrator of a retirement village—
to exercise all the functions of the operator of the retirement village, or
to exercise specified functions of the operator, or
to exercise all the functions other than specified functions of the operator.
The Secretary may apply for an order under this section only if—

the Secretary is of the opinion that the well-being or financial security of the residents of the retirement village concerned has been, or is likely to be, seriously affected by the continued operation of the retirement village by the operator, or

the Secretary is of the opinion that the operator of the retirement village concerned is wilfully and repeatedly acting in contravention of an order made by the Tribunal or a court in relation to the retirement village, or
the retirement village concerned is the subject of an existing order under this section.

For the purposes of determining whether an application for an order under this section should be made, the Secretary may appoint a person to inquire into, and report to the Secretary on, the well-being and financial security of the residents of a retirement village.
The Secretary is not to apply for an order appointing a person as an administrator under this Division unless the person has consented in writing to the appointment.

Without limiting the terms and conditions of the order of appointment of an administrator under this Division, the terms and conditions may exempt the administrator from the requirement to comply with such obligations of the operator as are specified or described in the order of appointment.

The operator of a retirement village must not, while an order under this Division is in force in respect of the village, exercise any of the functions of the operator that the administrator is authorised to exercise.
However, the appointment of an administrator does not relieve the operator of any of his or her liabilities under a village contract.

Subject to the terms of the appointment, a person appointed as an administrator of a retirement village must comply with all the obligations of the operator in relation to the functions that the person is authorised to exercise (including functions under a village contract) and is, in the exercise of those functions, taken to be the operator.

The expenses incurred by an administrator appointed under this Division in exercising the functions of the operator of a retirement village are payable from recurrent charges and such other funds as would be available to the operator for such expenses if the administrator had not been appointed.
Neither the Crown, the Minister nor the Secretary is liable for—
any expenses incurred by an administrator appointed under this Division to exercise the functions of the operator of a retirement village, or
any liability of an operator of a retirement village in respect of which an administrator is appointed.
Despite any other provision of this Act, an administrator appointed under this Division may, with the consent of the Secretary—
amend or revoke an approved annual budget, or
vary the recurrent charges payable by the residents of the retirement village, or
vary the services offered by the retirement village.
The Secretary may give consent under subsection (1) only if, in the opinion of the Secretary, the proposed revocation, variation or amendment is done for the purpose of—
assisting in the process of finding a new operator for the retirement village, or
ensuring the financial viability of the retirement village.
Nothing done by the administrator in accordance with this section is to be regarded as a breach of contract or otherwise as a civil wrong.
No compensation is payable to any person because of the operation of this section or anything done under this section.

An order made under this Division may be revoked or varied by the Supreme Court (whether or not on the application of the Secretary) and, unless sooner revoked, ceases to have effect at the expiration of such period after its making as may be specified in the order.
More than one order may be made under this Division in respect of the same retirement village.

If a receiver, or a receiver and manager, is appointed in respect of an operator of a retirement village, the person so appointed must (subject to the terms of the appointment) comply with the operator’s obligations under this Act as if that person were the operator.

The terms and conditions of appointment of a receiver, or a receiver and manager, may exempt the appointee from the requirement to comply with such obligations of the operator as are specified or described in the order of appointment.
This section does not apply to the extent that it is inconsistent with the Corporations Act 2001 of the Commonwealth.

heading.b: No personal liability of administrator, receiver or receiver and manager

block.txt: A matter or thing done or omitted to be done by an administrator, a receiver or a receiver and manager (or any person acting under the direction of the administrator, receiver or receiver and manager) does not, if the matter or thing was done or omitted in good faith for the purpose of executing this or any other Act, subject the administrator, receiver, receiver and manager or person so acting personally to any action, liability, claim or demand.
The operator of a retirement village is to determine a financial year for the village.
The financial year must be a period of 12 months commencing and ending on dates determined by the operator.
In this Division, an item of capital for which an operator of a retirement village is responsible means any item of capital within the retirement village other than an item of capital—
that is owned by a resident of the retirement village, or
that is association property under a community land scheme or common property under a strata scheme, or
that is of a class prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section.
For the purposes of this Division, maintenance or replacement of an item of capital is urgent if it is for the purpose of rectifying any of the following—
a burst water service,
a blocked or broken lavatory service,
a serious roof leak,
a gas leak,
a dangerous electrical fault,
flooding or serious flood damage,
serious storm or fire damage,
a failure or breakdown of the gas, electricity or water supply to residential premises within the retirement village,
a failure or breakdown of any essential service on the residential premises for hot water, cooking, heating or laundering,
any fault or damage that causes the retirement village to be unsafe or insecure,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Obligations of operator with respect to certain capital maintenance or replacement

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village is to maintain each item of capital for which the operator is responsible in a reasonable condition having regard to the following—
the age of the item,
the prospective life of the item,
the money paid to the operator by the residents under a village contract (including ingoing contributions).
If it is not practical to maintain an item of capital in accordance with this section, the operator may replace the item.

The operator of a retirement village must carry out the maintenance of, or replace, an item of capital for which the operator is responsible within a reasonable time after becoming aware of the need for the maintenance or replacement of the item.

heading.b: Obligations of residents with respect to capital maintenance or replacement

block.txt: A resident of a retirement village is to notify the operator of the retirement village of the need for maintenance to be carried out on, or the replacement of, an item of capital for which the operator is responsible and that is located within the resident’s residential premises as soon as the resident becomes aware of the need for the maintenance or replacement of the item.

A resident of a retirement village must reimburse the operator of the village in respect of any damage (other than fair wear and tear) caused by the resident to an item of capital for which the operator is responsible.

A resident of a retirement village must not hinder or obstruct the operator of the retirement village or a person authorised by the operator, from carrying out capital maintenance or capital replacement in respect of an item of capital for which the operator is responsible.

Section 67 sets out the circumstances in which an operator of a retirement village or a person authorised by the operator may enter residential premises in respect of which a person has a residence right.

heading.b: Resident may carry out urgent capital maintenance or replacement

block.txt: A resident of a retirement village may carry out capital maintenance or capital replacement in respect of an item of capital for which the operator of the retirement village is responsible if—
the maintenance or replacement of the item is urgent, and
the resident first gives the operator a reasonable opportunity to carry out the maintenance or replace the item.

A resident of a retirement village who carries out the maintenance of or replaces an item of capital in accordance with this section is entitled to be reimbursed by the operator of the retirement village for the reasonable costs incurred by the resident in doing so.

If the operator of a retirement village fails or refuses to reimburse a resident for costs in accordance with this section, the resident may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order requiring the operator to reimburse the resident for those costs.

heading.b: Tribunal may make orders for capital maintenance and replacement

block.txt: If a resident of a retirement village is of the opinion that the operator of the retirement village is not maintaining or replacing items of capital for which the operator is responsible when necessary, the resident may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing the operator—
to carry out specified maintenance of an item of capital within the time specified in the order, or
to replace a specified item of capital within the time specified in the order.

If the operator of a retirement village is of the opinion that a resident of the retirement village has caused damage to an item of capital for which the operator is responsible, the operator may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order directing the resident to reimburse the operator for the cost of the maintenance or replacement of the item of capital as a result of the damage.
Subsection (2) does not apply to damage caused by fair wear and tear.

heading.b: Funding of certain capital maintenance and capital replacement

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village may fund the cost of capital maintenance in respect of which the operator is responsible from the following sources—
the capital works fund for the retirement village (if any),
recurrent charges.
The operator of a retirement village must bear the cost of capital replacement in respect of an item of capital for which the operator is responsible.
This section does not authorise the funding of any of the following from the capital works fund or recurrent charges for the retirement village—
the construction of a new building or a new stage of the retirement village,
any work arising from the breach of a statutory warranty (within the meaning of the Home Building Act 1989) in respect of which proceedings may be commenced under Part 2C of that Act,
the depreciation of items of capital,
the refurbishment of vacant residential premises within the retirement village,
such other things as may be prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Capital maintenance to be included in proposed annual budget

block.txt: This section applies only if—
the operator of the retirement village is required to supply the residents of the retirement village with a proposed annual budget, and
the operator proposes to use any recurrent charges or any part of the capital works fund (if any) for the retirement village to fund capital maintenance.
The operator of a retirement village must, in the proposed annual budget—
list each item of capital maintenance that is proposed to be carried out, and
specify, in respect of each item, the expected cost, and
include, in respect of each item, any quotes that the operator has obtained, and
include provision for urgent capital maintenance.

If an approved annual budget provides for the setting aside of any part of the recurrent charges for the purpose of funding capital maintenance in a period that extends beyond the end of the financial year to which the budget relates, the operator of the retirement village must establish and maintain a capital works fund.
However, this section does not require that a separate fund be established in respect of each financial year.
A capital works fund must be held in an account with an authorised deposit-taking institution or as otherwise prescribed by the regulations.
The operator of a retirement village is to pay into the capital works fund—
such portion of the recurrent charges as may be required under an approved annual budget, and
any interest received from the investment of the whole, or any part of, the capital works fund.
The operator of a retirement village must not use money from the capital works fund except—
to meet the cost of capital maintenance, or

if the residents of the village consent to a proposal that the operator of the village distribute the whole, or any part, of the capital works fund that is not required to fund capital maintenance to the residents of the retirement village in equal shares—in accordance with that proposal, or
as prescribed by the regulations.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
A proposal under subsection (5) (b) may be made by the operator of the retirement village or the Residents Committee (if any).
If the residents consent under subsection (5) (b) to a proposal made by the Residents Committee, the operator may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order that—
the distribution is not to be made, or
approves or varies the proposed distribution.
In making an order under subsection (7) the Tribunal may consider the following—
the proportion of the capital works fund that is proposed to be distributed,
whether the proportion of the capital works fund that is proposed to be distributed is reasonably likely to be required to fund capital maintenance,
any other matter that the Tribunal considers appropriate.
The operator of a retirement village must cause the retirement village to be insured (and remain insured) in accordance with this section.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
The village must have insurance that—
covers the following—
damage,
costs incidental to the reinstatement or replacement of insured buildings,
public liability, and
provides for the reinstatement of property to its condition when new.
The regulations may prescribe a minimum amount of public liability insurance that is required under this section.
Insurance for damage and costs incidental to the reinstatement or replacement of insured buildings must cover the full replacement value of the retirement village.
Nothing in this section requires the operator of a retirement village to insure an item of capital other than an item of capital for which the operator is responsible.
The operator of a retirement village may fund insurance required under this section from recurrent charges if the cost of any such insurance is included in the approved annual budget.

heading.b: Operator not to sell items of capital to residents

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must not sell any item of capital for which the operator is responsible, or pass responsibility for any such item of capital (whether directly or indirectly), to a resident or prospective resident of the retirement village under a village contract or otherwise except as provided by the regulations.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

Any contract, agreement or scheme is unenforceable to the extent that it purports to sell or pass responsibility for the maintenance or replacement of items of capital in contravention of subsection (1).
This section does not apply to the sale of residential premises within a retirement village, including fixtures in any such premises.
An operator of a retirement village must, in accordance with the regulations, ensure that—
an asset management plan for the items of capital for which the operator is responsible is prepared, and
the asset management plan is kept up to date.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units (in the case of a corporation) or 50 penalty units (in any other case).

Section 189B enables the Secretary to issue guidelines to assist operators in complying with their obligations under this section. The Tribunal may take guidelines into account in determining whether there has been compliance with this section.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for or with respect to—
the preparation, duration and revision of asset management plans, and
the information to be recorded in asset management plans, including (but not limited to) information concerning any of the following—
the costs associated with both the maintenance or replacement of items of capital,
the reasons for decreases or increases in costs associated with both the maintenance or replacement of items of capital,
the frequency with which costs are incurred in respect of items of capital,
the expected lifespans of items of capital and expected maintenance and replacement requirements, and
the items of capital for which an asset management plan must be prepared.

In relation to a proposed variation in recurrent charges that is the first variation under a village contract, the prescribed CPI variation is, for the purposes of this Division, the variation that would result from the recurrent charges being increased in proportion to the difference between—
the Consumer Price Index published most recently before the village contract was entered into, and
the Consumer Price Index published most recently before the written notice of the proposed variation is given,
rounded to the nearest dollar.

In relation to a proposed variation in recurrent charges that is not the first variation under a village contract, the prescribed CPI variation is, for the purposes of this Division, the variation that would result from the recurrent charges being increased in proportion to the difference between—
the Consumer Price Index published most recently before those charges were last varied, and
the Consumer Price Index published most recently before the written notice of the proposed variation is given,
rounded to the nearest dollar.

heading.b: Operator to pay certain recurrent charges

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must pay, in relation to any new residential premises in the village, an amount equivalent to the recurrent charges for general services payable under a village contract in respect of comparable (or the most nearly comparable) premises in the village.
In this section, new residential premises means residential premises that are not and have never been the subject of a village contract.
A village contract may provide that any recurrent charges payable under it—
are to be varied at specified intervals (or on specified dates) according to a fixed formula (for example, in proportion to variations in the Consumer Price Index), or
may be varied otherwise than according to a fixed formula.

If a village contract provides for any recurrent charges payable under it to be varied otherwise than according to a fixed formula, the recurrent charges must not be varied more than once in any 12 month period. Any second or subsequent purported variation within that 12 month period is of no effect.
A village contract must not provide for more than one method of variation of the recurrent charges payable under it.

If a village contract provides for more than one method of variation of recurrent charges in contravention of subsection (3), the method that results in the lowest increase in recurrent charges is the applicable method.

heading.b: Recurrent charges varied by fixed formula

block.txt: If a village contract provides that recurrent charges are to be varied according to a fixed formula, the operator of the village must give at least 14 days’ written notice of the variation to the resident concerned.
The notice must specify—
the amount of the new recurrent charges, and
the date from which the new recurrent charges are payable, and
such other information as may be prescribed by the regulations.

A resident of the retirement village who is a party to a village contract referred to in subsection (1) is not required to pay any increase in his or her recurrent charges until notice of the increase is given as required by this section.

The operator of a retirement village must not increase (or attempt to increase) recurrent charges that are to be varied according to a fixed formula otherwise than in accordance with that formula and this section.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

heading.b: Recurrent charges varied otherwise than by fixed formula—not exceeding variation in CPI

block.txt: This section applies to the variation of recurrent charges payable under a village contract if—
the contract provides that recurrent charges are to be varied otherwise than in accordance with a fixed formula, and
the variation does not exceed the prescribed CPI variation.
The operator of a retirement village must give at least 14 days’ written notice of any proposed variation to the recurrent charges.
The notice must specify—
the amount of the new recurrent charges, and
the date from which the new recurrent charges are payable, and
such other information as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A resident of a retirement village is not required to pay any increase in his or her recurrent charges to which this section applies until notice of the increase is given as required by this section.
A notice given under this section may be cancelled by a later notice or a later notice may provide for a lesser increase than the increase specified in the earlier notice.

heading.b: Recurrent charges varied otherwise than by fixed formula—exceeding variation in CPI

block.txt: This section applies to a variation of recurrent charges payable under a village contract if—
the contract provides that recurrent charges are to be varied otherwise than in accordance with a fixed formula, and
the variation exceeds the prescribed CPI variation.
A provision to the effect that recurrent charges may be varied by “up to” a certain percentage is an example of such a provision.
The operator of a retirement village must give the resident concerned notice in accordance with this section at least 60 days before any proposed variation.
The notice must—
specify the amount of the proposed recurrent charges, and
specify the date from which it is intended that the proposed recurrent charges are to be payable, and
contain a brief explanation of the reasons for the proposed variation exceeding the prescribed CPI variation or the prescribed rate or amount (if any), and
include details of any action taken to minimise the proposed variation in recurrent charges, and
state that the variation will not take effect unless the residents concerned consent to the variation or the Tribunal orders that it take effect, and
contain such other information as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A notice given under this section may be cancelled by a later notice or a later notice may provide for a lesser increase than the increase specified in the earlier notice.
For the purposes of the date from which the proposed variation is to take effect, a later notice is taken to have been given on the date on which the earlier notice was given.
However, the period of 30 days specified in section 107 (2) commences, in relation to a later notice, on the date on which the later notice is actually given.
An operator who is the operator of more than one retirement village must deal with each village separately under this section.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

heading.b: Recurrent charges varied otherwise than by fixed formula to be increased in accordance with Act

block.txt: The operator of a retirement village must not increase (or attempt to increase) recurrent charges that are to be varied otherwise than according to a fixed formula if the increase would be—
beyond any upper limit specified in the relevant village contract, or
otherwise than in accordance with section 105A or 106.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
A variation does not take effect under section 106 unless—
the residents whose recurrent charges will be affected by the variation consent to the variation, or
the Tribunal orders under section 108 that the variation take effect.
The residents concerned must, within 30 days after receiving a notice under section 106—
meet, consider and vote on the proposed variation, and
advise the operator that they consent, or do not consent (as the case may be) to the variation.
If the operator is not advised as required by subsection (2) (b), the residents are taken to have refused consent to the variation.

The operator must provide such information in relation to the proposed variation as the Residents Committee (or, if there is no Residents Committee elected for the village, any resident) reasonably requests for the purpose of deciding whether consent should be given to the variation.

If the operator of a retirement village fails to provide information requested under subsection (4) within the time prescribed by the regulations, the Residents Committee (or a resident of the retirement village) may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order requiring the operator to provide the residents with the information specified in the order.
The regulations may prescribe—
the period within which information requested under subsection (4) must be provided, and
information that the operator of a retirement village is not required to provide despite a request under subsection (4).
An operator of a retirement village may apply to the Tribunal for (and the Tribunal may make) an order in respect of a proposed variation of recurrent charges if—
the consent of the residents of the retirement village is required before the proposed variation can take effect, and
the residents do not consent to the proposed variation under section 107.
The Tribunal may, on application by the operator—
order that the proposed variation is to take effect, with or without modification, or
order that the proposed variation is not to take effect.
An order under subsection (2) (a) may—
specify the date from which the variation is to take effect (which may be a date other than the date specified by the operator in the notice given under section 106), and
order that the recurrent charges are not to be further varied for a specified period, being a period that does not exceed 12 months.
In determining an application made under this section, the Tribunal may have regard to the following—
the general market level of recurrent charges paid at similar retirement villages in the locality of the retirement village concerned or a similar locality,
the level and cost of services and facilities provided for in the proposed annual budget or approved annual budget (as the case may be),
any proposed variations (including additions) to those services and facilities, being variations to which the residents have consented,
the cost of general services required to be provided by the operator,
the frequency and amount of past variations of the recurrent charges,

if the retirement village is subject to a community land scheme or strata scheme—the amounts of levies and other contributions payable by the residents under the Community Land Management Act 2021 or the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015,
any other relevant matter.

heading.b: Tribunal may order refund of recurrent charges in certain circumstances

block.txt: A resident of a retirement village may apply to the Tribunal for an order directing the refund of overpaid recurrent charges on any grounds, including the ground that an increase in the charges came into effect otherwise than in accordance with this Division.
The Tribunal may make an order directing a refund of all such overpaid recurrent charges.
An application under this section must be lodged no later than 12 months after the increase in the charges came into effect.
If payment of recurrent charges in a retirement village is made in person, any person who receives the payment must, without delay, give to the person making the payment a receipt for the payment.
Maximum penalty—5 penalty units.

If the payment is not made in person, the operator of the village must, as soon as practicable after receipt of the payment, prepare or cause to be prepared a receipt for the payment and make the receipt available for collection by the resident concerned or give it to the resident.
Maximum penalty—5 penalty units.
